roman_caeculus.name: Kindles and quenches fire, and is unharmed by it
roman_caeculus.notes: When his Vulcanian paternity was doubted at a public assembly he prayed to his father and fire encircled the crowd without harming them, proving the claim; he commands flame at will.

roman_remus.name: Reads the flight of birds (saw six vultures)
roman_remus.notes: In the augural contest for the founding Remus first saw six vultures, but Romulus then saw twelve and won by number; the priority-versus-quantity dispute precipitated the fatal quarrel.

sources.reference: Livy 1; Ovid, Fasti 4; Dionysius of Halicarnassus, Roman Antiquities 1

roman_juturna.name: Holds dominion over springs and running water
roman_juturna.notes: Made immortal by Jupiter and given lordship over springs, pools and rivers; invoked for healthful waters.

roman_juturna.name: Takes the form of her brother's charioteer to save him
roman_juturna.notes: Assumed the shape of Turnus' charioteer Metiscus, scattered the Latin ranks, and returned his lost sword to prolong his duel with Aeneas until a Dira drove her off.

roman_juturna.name: Spring and pool of Juturna (Lacus Iuturnae)
roman_juturna.notes: Her healing spring in the Roman Forum beside the Temple of Castor, where the Dioscuri were said to have watered their horses after Lake Regillus.

sources.reference: Ovid, Fasti 1; Dionysius of Halicarnassus, Roman Antiquities 6

roman_phaethon.name: Chariot of the Sun (currus Solis)
roman_phaethon.notes: The four-horse sun-chariot he wrung from his father Phoebus by oath and could not control; Jupiter's thunderbolt struck him from it to halt the world's burning.

roman_modius_fabidius.name: Sabine spear (curis)
roman_modius_fabidius.notes: His city Cures was named either for his father Quirinus or from the Sabine word curis, 'spear' — the weapon-emblem of the Marsian foundation.

roman_mercurius.name: Money-purse (marsupium)
roman_mercurius.notes: The merchant's coin-purse, a distinctively Roman commercial attribute marking Mercury as god of trade and gain.

roman_neptunus.name: Dolphin
roman_neptunus.notes: Carried as Neptune's attribute and companion of the sea-god.

roman_bellona.name: War-spear cast from the Columna Bellica
roman_bellona.notes: The fetial priest hurled a spear over the war-column before her temple to open hostilities; her own attribute is the hasta.

roman_bellona.name: Blood-red war-torch (fax)
roman_bellona.notes: Brandished as she rouses battle; depicted spattered with blood.

roman_ianus.name: Year-number reckoned on his fingers (CCC + LXV)
roman_ianus.notes: His statue showed the number 300 on the right hand and 65 on the left, marking the days of the solar year.

sources.reference: Livy 1; Dionysius of Halicarnassus, Roman Antiquities 2

roman_rhea_silvia.gloss: the Trojan woman (the older Ennian name)

sources.reference: Res Gestae Divi Augusti; Suetonius, Augustus
Res Gestae Divi Augusti; Suetonius, Augustus

roman_augustus.gloss: Son of the Deified (of Divus Iulius)

sources.reference: Coin legends; Res Gestae Divi Augusti

roman_livia_drusilla.gloss: the name and rank she took on Augustus's death and adoption into the gens Iulia

roman_mercurius.gloss: the Augustan Mercury (imperial-cult byname of trade-guilds)

roman_ianus.gloss: Janus Quirinus (peace-and-war title; the Geminus gates)

sources.reference: Cato, De Agri Cultura; Gellius; Macrobius, Saturnalia 1

roman_romulus.name: Quirinalia and the temple of Quirinus
roman_romulus.notes: After his apotheosis Romulus was worshipped as Quirinus, with a temple on the Quirinal and the flamen Quirinalis (one of the three major flamens); the Quirinalia fell on 17 February, the day of his vanishing at the Goat's Marsh.

sources.reference: Ovid, Fasti 2; Livy 10; Varro, De Lingua Latina 5

roman_romulus.name: Spolia opima at the temple of Iuppiter Feretrius
roman_romulus.notes: Romulus was the first of only three Romans to win the spolia opima, slaying Acron king of Caenina and dedicating the spoils to Iuppiter Feretrius, whose temple he founded as their repository.

roman_augustus.name: Cult of Divus Augustus (flamen, sodales, temple, Augustalia)
roman_augustus.notes: On his consecration the Senate created the flamen Augustalis (Germanicus the first) and the sodales Augustales; the temple of Divus Augustus on the Palatine slope was dedicated under Caligula in 37 CE, with Livia as his priestess, and the Augustalia games were held in October. During his lifetime his Genius and numen were already worshipped and the Lares Augusti set up at the crossroads.

sources.reference: Tacitus, Annals 1; Cassius Dio 56; Suetonius, Augustus; Ovid, Fasti 5

roman_caesar_dictator.name: Cult of Divus Iulius (flamen, temple, sidus Iulium)
roman_caesar_dictator.notes: Deified by decree in 42 BCE with Mark Antony as the first flamen Divi Iulii; the temple of Divus Iulius was raised in the Forum on the site of his cremation and dedicated by Octavian in 29 BCE. The comet (sidus Iulium) that blazed during his funeral games was read as his soul received among the gods, and a star was set on his statue's brow.

sources.reference: Suetonius, Julius; Cassius Dio 47; Pliny, Natural History 2; Ovid, Metamorphoses 15

roman_livia_drusilla.name: Cult of Diva Augusta
roman_livia_drusilla.notes: Claudius deified his grandmother as Diva Augusta in 42 CE; her statue was set beside Augustus's in his temple, the Vestals and a priestess tended her cult, an elephant-drawn carriage bore her image at the games, and women were to invoke her in their oaths.

roman_caligula.name: Living self-deification cult
roman_caligula.cadence: during his reign, from ca. 39-40 CE; never officially confirmed
roman_caligula.notes: Caligula set up a temple to his own godhead with priests and exotic victims, containing a life-size gold image of himself dressed each day to match his own clothing; he sought worship as Jupiter and ordered a colossal statue of himself placed in the Temple at Jerusalem. He was not officially deified after his murder, his memory effectively suppressed.

sources.reference: Suetonius, Caligula; Cassius Dio 59; Philo, Legatio ad Gaium; Josephus, Antiquities 18

roman_juturna.name: Iuturnalia at the Lacus Iuturnae
roman_juturna.notes: Festival of Juturna on 11 January; those whose craft used water honoured her at her Forum shrine and at her temple in the Campus Martius vowed by Lutatius Catulus.

sources.reference: Varro, De Lingua Latina 6; Servius on Aeneid 12

roman_ceres.name: Cerialia and the ludi Ceriales
roman_ceres.notes: Plebeian-aedile games in the Circus Maximus; on the final day foxes with burning brands tied to their tails were loosed in the circus.

roman_ceres.name: Porca praecidanea and the ieiunium Cereris
roman_ceres.cadence: pig-offering before harvest; fast instituted 191 BCE, later annual 4 October
roman_ceres.notes: A sow (porca) was sacrificed to Ceres before reaping; the Fast of Ceres was instituted on Sibylline advice in 191 BCE.

roman_liber.name: Liberalia
roman_liber.notes: Day on which boys assumed the toga virilis; ivy-crowned old priestesses sat at crossroads with portable braziers selling honey-cakes (liba) and sacrificing for buyers. A phallus-cart procession to bless the fields is attested for Lavinium.

sources.reference: Ovid, Fasti 3; Augustine, De Civitate Dei 7 (Lavinium rite, citing Varro)

roman_faunus.name: Faunalia
roman_faunus.notes: Country folk brought a kid, wine and incense to a rural altar with dancing; a second Faunalia on 13 February attached to his Tiber-island temple (dedicated 194 BCE).

roman_faunus.name: Lupercalia
roman_faunus.notes: Luperci, girt in goatskins, ran striking passers-by (especially women, for fertility) with goatskin thongs after the sacrifice of goats at the Lupercal; Livy names Inuus as the god of the rite.

roman_pomona.name: Flamen Pomonalis and the sacred grove (Pomonal)
roman_pomona.cadence: served by a dedicated state priest
roman_pomona.notes: Pomona had her own flamen, the lowest of the flamines minores because she presides over the least of crops (tree-fruit); her sacred grove, the Pomonal, lay on the Via Ostiensis. No festival or temple is attested.

sources.reference: Festus, De Verborum Significatu; Varro, De Lingua Latina 5

roman_ops.name: Opiconsivia and Opalia
roman_ops.cadence: annual, Opiconsivia 25 August; Opalia 19 December (within Saturnalia)
roman_ops.notes: Her restricted sacrarium in the Regia could be entered only by the Vestals and the state priest; worshippers invoked her seated, hands touching the earth, since her seat is within the ground.

sources.reference: Varro, De Lingua Latina 6; Macrobius, Saturnalia 1

roman_bona_dea.name: Nocturnal December rite at a magistrate's house
roman_bona_dea.notes: Held by night at the house of a magistrate cum imperio, led by his wife and the Vestals with all men excluded; the 62 BCE rite at Caesar's house was profaned by Clodius in disguise. Wine was brought under the name lac (milk) in a honey-jar (mellarium), myrtle was forbidden, and tame snakes were kept.

sources.reference: Cicero, Ad Atticum; Plutarch, Caesar; Macrobius, Saturnalia 1

roman_bona_dea.name: May temple-festival on the Aventine
roman_bona_dea.notes: Rite at her Aventine temple sub saxo; medicinal herbs were kept and dispensed there.

roman_mercurius.name: Mercuralia at the Aqua Mercurii
roman_mercurius.notes: Merchants drew water from the spring of Mercury by the Porta Capena and sprinkled themselves and their wares with a laurel branch, praying for absolution of past and future commercial perjuries; his temple on the Aventine slope (dedicated 495 BCE) faced the Circus Maximus and the collegium mercatorum was founded with it.

roman_neptunus.name: Neptunalia
roman_neptunus.notes: In high summer Romans raised leafy branch-huts called umbrae and feasted under them with spring-water and wine, a rite for water in drought; the closely linked Consualia honoured Neptunus Equester with horse-races at an underground altar by the Circus Maximus.

roman_pluto.name: Night-sacrifice at the Tarentum altar
roman_pluto.cadence: the Republican Ludi Tarentini/Saeculares (notably 249 and 207 BCE)
roman_pluto.notes: A buried altar of Dis Pater and Proserpina in the Campus Martius was uncovered for the games; black victims were offered to them by night.

roman_proserpina.name: Greek-rite cult of Ceres and Proserpina
roman_proserpina.cadence: established 205 BCE on the Aventine; shared night-rite at the Tarentum altar
roman_proserpina.notes: The Hellenized mystery cult of Ceres and Proserpina with Greek priestesses was brought in 205 BCE on Sibylline advice; she also shared the buried Tarentum altar with Dis Pater for the Republican Saecular night-sacrifice.

sources.reference: Livy (205 BCE Aventine cult); Valerius Maximus 2; Zosimus, Historia Nova 2

roman_luna.name: Temple on the Aventine and shrine of Noctiluca on the Palatine
roman_luna.notes: Her Aventine temple (ascribed to Servius Tullius, below Diana's) burned in the fire of 64 CE; on the Palatine the shrine of Luna Noctiluca was said to glow by night. Luna was paired with Sol in the circus games.

sources.reference: Tacitus, Annals 15; Ovid, Fasti 3; Varro, De Lingua Latina 5

roman_fortuna.name: Lot-oracle of Fortuna Primigenia at Praeneste
roman_fortuna.notes: Oak lots kept in an olive-wood chest were drawn by a boy at the famous sanctuary; Cicero records the founding legend of Numerius Suffustius and his own scepticism.

roman_fortuna.name: Fors Fortuna festival across the Tiber
roman_fortuna.notes: Plebs and slaves travelled by boat down the Tiber, garlanded and with wine, to the two ancient riverside temples ascribed to Servius Tullius.

sources.reference: Ovid, Fasti 6; Dionysius of Halicarnassus, Roman Antiquities 4

roman_ianus.name: Ianus Geminus (gates open in war, shut in peace)
roman_ianus.cadence: doors opened in war, closed in peace (closed thrice under Augustus)
roman_ianus.notes: The bronze double-gateway in the Forum whose doors stood open while Rome was at war; Augustus closed them three times. Janus was named first in every prayer and sacrifice.

sources.reference: Augustus, Res Gestae 13; Livy 1; Ovid, Fasti 1

roman_ianus.name: Agonium of 9 January
roman_ianus.notes: The rex sacrorum sacrificed a ram to Janus at the Regia; the cake libum ianual was offered to him, and the month Ianuarius and the New Year were his.

sources.reference: Ovid, Fasti 1; Varro, De Lingua Latina 6; Festus

roman_mars.name: October Equus and the Equirria
roman_mars.cadence: Equirria 27 February and 14 March; October Equus 15 October
roman_mars.notes: After a chariot-race on the Campus Martius the right-hand horse of the winning team was speared for Mars; its head was contested between the Subura and Sacra Via, its tail carried to the Regia so the blood dripped on the hearth. The Equirria were his horse-races, the Tubilustrium (23 March) purified the war-trumpets.

sources.reference: Festus, De Verborum Significatu; Ovid, Fasti 2-3; Plutarch, Quaestiones Romanae

roman_mars.name: Ambarvalia lustration with the suovetaurilia
roman_mars.notes: The fields were purified by leading a pig, sheep and bull (sus, ovis, taurus) around them with a prayer to Mars Pater; Cato preserves the farm-prayer formula.

sources.reference: Cato, De Agri Cultura; Virgil, Georgics 1

roman_bellona.name: Temple of Bellona and the Columna Bellica
roman_bellona.cadence: vowed 296 BCE by Appius Claudius Caecus
roman_bellona.notes: Her temple by the Circus Flaminius lay outside the pomerium, where the Senate met returning generals awaiting a triumph and foreign envoys; before it stood the war-column over which the fetial priest hurled a spear to declare war. The ecstatic blood-rite of the Bellonarii belongs to her later fusion with the Anatolian goddess Ma.

sources.reference: Livy 10; Ovid, Fasti 6; (Bellonarii) Lucan, Bellum Civile; Juvenal, Satura 6

attributes.name: Augur's striped trabea and lituus
attributes.notes: Shown as the founding augur in the purple-striped trabea holding the crook-staff (lituus).

sacredAnimals.name: She-wolf suckling the twins (lupa)
sacredAnimals.notes: The Lupa Romana nursing Romulus and Remus at the Lupercal, the canonical foundation image.

sources.reference: Livy 1; Ovid, Fasti 2; Dionysius of Halicarnassus, Roman Antiquities 1

sacredPlants.name: Ficus Ruminalis
sacredPlants.notes: The sacred wild fig by the Lupercal, beneath which the twins' cradle grounded.

sources.reference: Livy 1; Pliny, Natural History 15; Tacitus, Annals 13

attributes.name: Shepherd among the flocks
attributes.notes: Reared as a herdsman; shares the she-wolf scene with his twin but has no attribute of his own.

attributes.name: Sleeping Vestal visited by Mars
attributes.notes: The standard relief and sarcophagus type: a reclining Vestal approached by Mars descending, often with Amor, Somnus and a river-god present.

sources.reference: Roman sarcophagus reliefs (e.g. Sarcofago Mattei); LIMC 'Rhea Silvia'

attributes.name: Weak, smoke-shrunk eyes
attributes.notes: The hearth-smoke dimmed his eyes, giving him the name Caeculus, 'little blind one' (from caecus); his sacred element is fire and the hearth.

attributes.name: Falling youth and runaway sun-chariot
attributes.notes: Depicted plunging from the careering four-horse chariot struck by Jupiter's bolt.

attributes.name: Heliades weeping amber as poplars
attributes.notes: His sisters, mourning by the Eridanus (Po), were turned to poplars weeping amber; his kinsman Cycnus became a swan.

attributes.name: Cuirassed Prima Porta type and veiled Pontifex Maximus type
attributes.notes: The breastplated imperator statue (with the returned Parthian standards and Cupid on a dolphin) and the capite velato priest type.

sources.reference: Prima Porta Augustus; Roman statuary tradition

attributes.name: Civic oak-crown and flanking laurels
attributes.notes: The corona civica and two laurels voted for his door in 27 BCE, standard on his coinage.

sources.reference: Res Gestae Divi Augusti; Ovid, Fasti 1; Cassius Dio 53

attributes.name: Capricorn birth-sign emblem
attributes.notes: He publicized Capricorn (his natal-moon sign) and struck it on silver, often with cornucopia, globe and rudder.

attributes.name: Consecratio eagle and radiate crown
attributes.notes: An eagle released from his funeral pyre bore his soul to heaven; Divus Augustus coinage shows the radiate crown.

attributes.name: Comet-star (sidus Iulium)
attributes.notes: The eight-rayed star set above his statue's brow and struck on DIVVS IVLIVS coinage.

sources.reference: Pliny, Natural History 2; Suetonius, Julius; Ovid, Metamorphoses 15

attributes.name: Laurel wreath
attributes.notes: The perpetual right to wear the laurel crown; he was the first living Roman with his portrait on the coinage.

attributes.name: Appearing in the costumes of the gods
attributes.notes: He showed himself publicly with the attributes of Jupiter (thunderbolt), Neptune (trident), Hercules (lion-skin and club), Bacchus, Apollo and Mercury, and even in the dress of goddesses such as Venus.

attributes.name: Water-nymph with urn
attributes.notes: Depicted as a spring-nymph associated with the welling water of her Forum pool.

sources.reference: Cato, De Agri Cultura; Ovid, Fasti 1

sacredAnimals.name: He-goat (caper)
sacredAnimals.notes: Slain at the altar because it gnaws the vine.

attributes.name: Goat-horns and goat-legs
attributes.notes: Shown with horns, shaggy legs and tail through his identification with Pan.

attributes.name: Lap and arms laden with fruit
attributes.notes: Holds and tends ripe orchard-fruit; her name is from pomum.

attributes.name: Seated goddess touching the earth
attributes.notes: Invoked seated with hands on the ground; shown with sceptre, cornucopia and corn-spray.

sacredAnimals.name: Snake (serpens/anguis)
sacredAnimals.notes: Tame snakes were kept in her temple precinct.

sacredPlants.name: Vine (wine called lac); myrtle forbidden
sacredPlants.notes: Wine was admitted under the name of milk while myrtle was banned from her rite.

sacredAnimals.name: Cockerel (gallus)
sacredAnimals.notes: Herald of the day, fitting the messenger-god.

sacredAnimals.name: Horse (equus)
sacredAnimals.notes: As Neptunus Equester, patron and giver of horses, honoured at the Consualia races.

sources.reference: Livy 1; Dionysius of Halicarnassus, Roman Antiquities 2

sacredAnimals.name: Black victims (black sheep and bull)
sacredAnimals.notes: Black animals sacrificed to him by night at the Tarentum.

sacredPlants.name: Cypress (cupressus)
sacredPlants.notes: The funerary tree of the dead, planted at tombs and in mourning.

attributes.name: Torch (fax)
attributes.notes: Torches mark her abduction and her mother's search.

sacredPlants.name: Narcissus
sacredPlants.notes: The flower she was gathering when seized by Dis.

attributes.name: Crescent moon and billowing veil
attributes.notes: Wears the crescent on her brow with a wind-blown veil arched overhead, often carrying a torch.

sources.reference: Roman numismatic and relief iconography of Luna

attributes.name: Globe (globus)
attributes.notes: Stands on or rests her foot upon a sphere, signifying dominion over the world's chances.

attributes.name: Two opposed faces (bifrons)
attributes.notes: One face looks forward and one back; shown on the Republican as.

sacredAnimals.name: Woodpecker (picus Martius)
sacredAnimals.notes: Sacred to Mars and a guide-animal of the ver sacrum; it fed the infant twins. The Picentes were named from the picus.

sources.reference: Ovid, Fasti 3; Plutarch, Quaestiones Romanae; Festus

sacredAnimals.name: Wolf (lupus)
sacredAnimals.notes: His sacred beast; the she-wolf suckled Romulus and Remus and the Hirpini were named from the wolf that led their ver sacrum.

attributes.name: Helmeted and blood-spattered, with spear and scourge
attributes.notes: Strides or drives into battle wielding spear, torch and bloody whip.

sources.reference: Virgil, Aeneid 8; Lucan, Bellum Civile; Statius, Thebaid
